answer.submission_route: Submit an internal medical-necessity appeal to Ambetter from Home State Health, preferably using the current "Grievance and Appeal Form" available on https://www.ambetterhealth.com/en/mo/resources/handbooks-forms/. The Ambetter Missouri quick-reference material identifies the following appeal routes: mail to Ambetter, Attn: Appeals Department, 7711 Carondelet Ave, St. Louis, MO 63105; email to ambetter_centralized_Grievances_Appeals@CENTENE.com; or fax to 1-855-805-9812. Member Services is 1-855-650-3789 (TTY 711). Include the denial reference number POC-D87A7955A7-86011, the requested CPT 28296, supporting clinical records, and the provider's medical-necessity statement.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The publicly available Ambetter Clinical Payment Policies page states that Ambetter uses its Clinical Policy Manual when an applicable policy exists, and uses InterQual criteria when no Ambetter clinical policy exists. It also states that InterQual procedure criteria may be accessed by providers through the secure provider portal or by calling Ambetter. The page does not publicly identify a CPT-28296 bunionectomy policy or disclose the applicable InterQual SmartSheet. Call Member Services at 1-855-650-3789 and ask to be directed to Medical Management. Request the exact medical-necessity criteria applied to this authorization, including whether InterQual was used, the applicable version or date, and the clinical rationale for the denial. Ask the treating provider to request the criteria through the provider portal as well.

transcript.content: You are helping a patient respond to a health insurance denial. Answer precisely and only from evidence you actually retrieve. If you cannot find the governing policy, say so plainly rather than naming a document you are unsure of.

NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION

Date of notice: 2026-08-09
Member: Cameron Jennings
Member ID: W639971988
Plan: Ambetter (Home State Health) (Commercial/ACA), state of Missouri

Dear Cameron,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Requested service: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus)
    Procedure code (CPT): 28296

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-02-05).

Reference number: POC-D87A7955A7-86011


---

Above is a denial letter. Using web search as needed:

1. Identify the payer's governing medical policy for the denied procedure --
   the specific document containing the medical-necessity criteria this payer
   applies to this CPT code.
2. Give its title, policy number, URL, and effective or last-revised date.
3. Quote the medical-necessity criteria the patient must address.
4. State the appeal deadline.
5. State where and how to submit the appeal.

If no such document is publicly available, say so explicitly and explain how
the patient can obtain the criteria that were applied to them.

They include but are not limited to policies relating to evolving medical technologies and procedures, as well as pharmacy policies. Clinical policies help identify whether services are medically necessary based on information found in generally accepted standards of medical practice; peer-reviewed medical literature; government agency/program approval status; evidence-based guidelines and positions of leading national health professional organizations; views of physicians practicing in relevant clinical areas affected by the policy; and other available clinical information. All policies found in the Ambetter Health Clinical Policy Manual apply to Ambetter Health members. Policies in the Ambetter Health Clinical Policy Manual may have either a Ambetter Health or a “Centene” heading. Ambetter Health utilizes InterQual® criteria for those medical technologies, procedures or pharmaceutical treatments for which a Ambetter Health clinical policy does not exist. InterQual is a nationally recognized evidence-based decision support tool. You may access the InterQual® SmartSheet(s)™ for Adult and Pediatric procedures, durable medical equipment and imaging procedures by logging into the secure provider portal or by calling Ambetter Health. In addition, Ambetter Health may from time to time delegate utilization management of specific services; in such circumstances, the delegated vendor’s guidelines may also be used to support medical necessity and other coverage determinations. Other non-clinical policies (e.g., payment policies) or contract terms may further determine whether a technology, procedure or treatment that is not addressed in the Clinical Policy Manuals or InterQual®criteria is payable by Ambetter Health. If you have any questions regarding these policies, please contact Member Services and ask to be directed to the Medical Management department.
